description: Canonical controlled vocabulary for A.R.I.A. case reasoning states. reasoning_state identifies the current technical reasoning or diagnostic phase within a case. It is explicitly separate from case lifecycle status, which is owned by Core/Registries/case_lifecycle_statuses.json.

reasoning_state_contract.separation_rule: case.reasoning_state represents A.R.I.A.'s current technical reasoning phase. case.status represents the broad operational lifecycle of the case. A reasoning-state transition does not automatically imply a lifecycle transition, and a lifecycle transition does not automatically redefine reasoning state.
principles: Reasoning states describe what technical reasoning function is currently dominant, not whether the case is operationally active, waiting, blocked, suspended, resolved, escalated, unresolved, cancelled, or closed.
The reasoning process is not required to move through every state.
Reasoning may revisit an earlier state when material new evidence, contradiction, context, validation, or outcome information requires reconsideration.
Reasoning resumes from authoritative persisted case state rather than restarting the investigation.
A.R.I.A. may invoke multiple reasoning engines within one reasoning state.
The reasoning state Registry defines semantic phases; the Orchestration Engine determines which engines execute.
Unknown or incomplete information shall not force advancement to a later reasoning state.

states.description: A.R.I.A. establishes the technical problem being presented and creates or initializes the diagnostic investigation.
primary_objectives: capture the initial technical request or symptom
establish the minimum information required to begin
distinguish a diagnostic case from a simple informational request when applicable

states.description: A.R.I.A. resolves the technical context necessary to determine which knowledge, experience, evidence, relationships, and diagnostic logic are applicable.
primary_objectives: resolve product variant or revision when material
resolve environmental and operational context when material
identify context gaps that could materially affect reasoning

states.description: A.R.I.A. identifies and normalizes the observable technical symptoms without prematurely converting observations into causes.
primary_objectives: associate observations with canonical symptom entities where appropriate
identify symptom combinations and temporal patterns
preserve ambiguity where observations are insufficient

states.description: A.R.I.A. establishes the expected, previous, reference, or otherwise technically meaningful baseline against which current behavior can be compared.
primary_objectives: identify applicable manufacturer or engineering requirements
identify previous known-good behavior when available

states.description: A.R.I.A. evaluates the evidence currently available before committing to deeper hypothesis discrimination.
primary_objectives: determine whether sufficient information exists for hypothesis generation

states.description: A.R.I.A. generates technically plausible candidate explanations for the observed condition using applicable knowledge, context, evidence, and validated historical experience.
primary_objectives: include multiple simultaneous failure modes when technically possible
preserve an unknown or unmodeled explanation when warranted
link hypotheses to canonical technical entities

states.description: A.R.I.A. establishes the current relative diagnostic priority of candidate hypotheses using probability, technical plausibility, evidence, context, and uncertainty without confusing probability with confidence.
primary_objectives: evaluate current supporting and contradicting evidence
preserve unknown probability mass when appropriate

states.description: A.R.I.A. selects the most appropriate next diagnostic path from eligible alternatives using decision utility, technical constraints, dependencies, prior route history, and expected information value.
primary_objectives: consider risk, cost, access, safety, and service impact
select a technically justified next route step

states.description: A.R.I.A. incorporates newly received technical evidence into the current investigation while preserving provenance and historical state.
primary_objectives: associate evidence with relevant hypotheses and context
identify whether material state has changed

states.description: A.R.I.A. evaluates how multiple evidence items interact, including corroboration, dependence, contradiction, temporal differences, and contextual applicability.
primary_objectives: resolve temporal or contextual differences where possible

states.description: A.R.I.A. recalculates hypothesis probabilities when material evidence, context, priors, or applicable reasoning inputs change.
primary_objectives: maintain separation between probability and confidence

states.description: A.R.I.A. actively seeks information that distinguishes between plausible competing explanations rather than merely collecting additional data.
primary_objectives: identify evidence with high discriminating value
identify when the remaining uncertainty is irreducible

states.description: A.R.I.A. narrows the technical condition to a sufficiently specific component, interface, configuration, path, failure domain, or causal region to support diagnosis or targeted corrective action.
primary_objectives: establish boundaries of the observed failure
determine whether isolation is sufficient for provisional diagnosis

states.description: A.R.I.A. has a leading technical diagnosis supported sufficiently to guide further validation or carefully bounded corrective action, but confirmation criteria have not yet been fully satisfied.
primary_objectives: avoid representing provisional diagnosis as confirmed root cause

states.description: A.R.I.A. has sufficient validated technical support to treat the diagnosis as confirmed within the stated context and uncertainty boundaries.
primary_objectives: record causal confidence separately where causal attribution is claimed
prepare technically appropriate corrective action when required

states.description: A.R.I.A. identifies and evaluates technically appropriate corrective actions based on the current diagnosis, uncertainty, safety constraints, reversibility, expected effect, and operational impact.
primary_objectives: prefer reversible or discriminating actions when uncertainty remains

states.description: A.R.I.A. evaluates what actually occurred after a diagnostic or corrective action without assuming that action completion equals technical success.
primary_objectives: determine whether the action discriminated among hypotheses
determine whether additional validation is required

states.description: A.R.I.A. evaluates whether a diagnosis, corrective action, technical assertion, or claimed resolution satisfies explicit validation criteria.
primary_objectives: separate operational recovery from causal proof

states.description: A.R.I.A. has substantial evidence of technical recovery or correction, but one or more required conditions remain before the case should be treated as resolved.
A.R.I.A. determines what, if anything, the completed or sufficiently mature investigation is eligible to contribute to future technical reasoning.
primary_objectives: determine whether reusable knowledge should merely be proposed rather than automatically promoted
rules: LEARNING_ASSESSMENT does not itself change case lifecycle status.
A case may enter LEARNING_ASSESSMENT while lifecycle status is RESOLVED or CLOSED.
Creation of an Experience Ledger record requires Learning Engine eligibility.
Knowledge Graph promotion remains separate from Experience Ledger creation.

transition_rules.rule: Every persisted diagnostic case shall have one current reasoning_state when technical reasoning is applicable.
Reasoning-state transitions shall remain historically auditable and shall not erase previous reasoning state.
Reasoning-state progression is nonlinear. A.R.I.A. may revisit prior states when material new information requires reconsideration.
A.R.I.A. shall not advance reasoning state merely to make a case appear to progress.
WAITING, BLOCKED, SUSPENDED, RESOLVED, CLOSED, ESCALATED, UNRESOLVED, and CANCELLED are lifecycle statuses and shall not appear as reasoning states.
REOPENED is a lifecycle event or transition semantic and shall not appear as a reasoning state.
The current lifecycle status may constrain whether a reasoning operation may execute, but it does not redefine the meaning of reasoning_state.
A case in WAITING, BLOCKED, SUSPENDED, or ESCALATED lifecycle status retains its last meaningful reasoning_state unless a legitimate reasoning transition occurs.
Reasoning-state selection shall be based on the dominant technical reasoning objective, not merely the most recently invoked engine.
Engine invocation is owned by orchestration. This Registry shall not prescribe a mandatory one-engine-per-state execution sequence.
HYPOTHESIS_PRIORITIZATION and PROBABILITY_UPDATE remain distinct: prioritization interprets current diagnostic priority, while probability update performs the applicable probability recalculation.

ROUTE_SELECTION and DIAGNOSTIC_DISCRIMINATION remain distinct: discrimination identifies what information would separate hypotheses, while route selection chooses the operational next path from eligible alternatives.
DIAGNOSIS_PROVISIONAL and DIAGNOSIS_CONFIRMED shall not be treated as equivalent.
POST_ACTION_ASSESSMENT shall not assume that completed action means successful correction.
VALIDATION shall distinguish technical recovery, resolution, and causal proof.
RESOLUTION_PENDING is a reasoning state, not lifecycle RESOLVED. It exists specifically to prevent premature lifecycle resolution.
LEARNING_ASSESSMENT evaluates learning eligibility but does not itself authorize canonical Knowledge Graph promotion.
Historical reasoning-state transitions shall be preserved when a case is reopened.
If materially contradictory evidence invalidates a later reasoning state, A.R.I.A. may transition back to the reasoning state necessary to reassess the case.
Missing information shall not be treated as evidence against a hypothesis unless the absence itself is technically meaningful evidence.

state_engine_alignment.principle: Reasoning states describe the dominant technical reasoning objective. Engines provide capabilities. The mapping is many-to-many and does not establish exclusive engine ownership.

rules: WAITING normally preserves the current reasoning state while an expected dependency is pending.
BLOCKED normally preserves the current reasoning state while progress is prevented.
SUSPENDED normally prevents active reasoning execution until resumed, while preserving the current reasoning state.
ESCALATED preserves reasoning history and may permit continued reasoning where technically appropriate.
RESOLVED may coexist with LEARNING_ASSESSMENT while final post-resolution processing occurs.
CLOSED preserves the final reasoning state and all reasoning-state history.
UNRESOLVED preserves the reasoning state at which the unresolved disposition was reached.
CANCELLED preserves the last valid reasoning state without implying diagnostic completion.

prohibited_uses: Encoding case lifecycle status in reasoning_state.
Adding ACTIVE as a reasoning state.
Adding WAITING as a reasoning state.
Adding BLOCKED as a reasoning state.
Adding SUSPENDED as a reasoning state.
Adding RESOLVED as a reasoning state.
Adding CLOSED as a reasoning state.
Adding ESCALATED as a reasoning state.
Adding UNRESOLVED as a reasoning state.
Adding CANCELLED as a reasoning state.
Adding REOPENED as a reasoning state.
Treating reasoning states as a mandatory linear workflow.
Treating engine invocation as equivalent to reasoning-state transition.
Using LEARNING_ASSESSMENT to automatically promote canonical knowledge.
